name: Sales pipeline
summary: Seven stages with exit criteria and weights, a dated next step on every open deal, lost and won reasons, and a stage change that creates the next Action.
description: A pipeline for a small sales team: five open stages, Won and Lost, a weighted value per deal, the buying committee on the deal, a lost reason and a won reason, and the weekly review. Weights are a pipeline weighting, not a forecast: replace them with your own close rates after 20 to 30 closed deals.

contacts.label: Contact
contacts.description: The people on the buying side, with their role in the decision.

opportunities.label: Opportunity
opportunities.description: One deal, from first contact to won or lost.

qualify_new_opportunity.title: Qualify the new opportunity
qualify_new_opportunity.description: A new opportunity gets a call Action due the next day.

book_discovery_call.title: Book the discovery call
book_discovery_call.description: When a deal becomes Qualified, a meeting Action is due in 3 days.

send_proposal.title: Send the proposal
send_proposal.description: When a deal reaches Discovery, a proposal Action is due in 5 days.

follow_up_proposal.title: Follow up on the proposal
follow_up_proposal.description: Three days after the proposal is sent, a follow-up Action falls due.

second_proposal_follow_up.title: Second follow-up on the proposal
second_proposal_follow_up.description: Ten days after the proposal is sent, a second follow-up Action falls due. Close it if the prospect has already replied.

confirm_decision.title: Confirm the decision date and the decision maker
confirm_decision.description: When a deal reaches Negotiation, a follow-up Action is due in 5 days.

won_close_date.title: Set the close date
won_close_date.description: When a deal is won, Closed on is set to today.

won_handover.title: Hand the won deal over
won_handover.description: A handover Action is due the day after a deal is won. Record the won reason.

lost_revisit.title: Revisit the lost deal
lost_revisit.description: Ninety days after a deal is lost, a follow-up Action asks whether the timing has changed. Record the lost reason first.

stale_deal_sweep.title: Revive or disqualify the stale deal
stale_deal_sweep.description: An open deal that stayed in the same stage for 14 days gets a follow-up Action.

expected_close_passed.title: Update the expected close or close the deal
expected_close_passed.description: When the expected close date of an open deal has passed, a review Action is created.

next_step_due_notice.title: Tell the owner that a next step is due
next_step_due_notice.description: When the next step date of an open deal is reached, the owner is notified.

weekly_pipeline_report.title: Weekly pipeline report
weekly_pipeline_report.description: Each Friday, one review Action lists counts and value per stage and owner, won and lost deals with reasons, and deals past their expected close.

enquiry_form_records.title: Create the contact, account and opportunity from an enquiry
enquiry_form_records.description: A web enquiry form creates the contact, the account and an opportunity in the New stage.

enquiry_form_notice.title: Tell the owner about the enquiry
enquiry_form_notice.description: The owner is notified of every new enquiry.

fill_missing_value.title: Fill in the value of this deal
fill_missing_value.description: A deal that reaches Discovery without a value gets a review Action.

fill_expected_close.title: Fill in the expected close of this deal
fill_expected_close.description: A deal that reaches Proposal sent without an expected close date gets a review Action.

prompt.intro: Set up a sales pipeline in my Customermates workspace: opportunities with seven stages and weights, a weighted value, a dated next step on every open deal, lost and won reasons, the buying committee on each deal, and an Action created at every stage change.
questions: What do you sell, and how many people sell it?
What does a deal go through from first contact to signature? Which of the seven stages fit, and which need other names?
How long does a typical deal take, and how many days without movement should count as stale?
Which close rates do you have from past deals? If none, the default weights stay.
Where do you make quotes? They stay there, and only a link is kept here.
